transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I... well, I guess I'm here because... I just can't shake this thought. I've been an electrician for years, you know? And... if all that experience couldn't keep my own brother safe, then... I don't know. I just feel like I'm a danger to anybody who works with me. Or even anyone who lives under my roof.
Can you tell me more about what happened with your brother, and how often you find yourself thinking about it or blaming yourself for it?

I... I'd really rather not get into the details of the accident right now. It's just... it's a lot. 

But as for how often I think about it... it happens all the time. I'll just be, you know, in the middle of wiring a panel at work. Or... or I'll be at home and hear my nephew shut the garage door. And suddenly I'm... I'm right back there. I can smell the smoke, and... I see him. It's like the whole job site just drops out from under me. 

It just... it doesn't stop.
Do you find yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself not just for what happened, but in other areas of your life as well?

I don't know about other areas of my life. It's mostly just... this constant feeling. Like this heavy mix of guilt and... anger, I guess. It just sits in my chest all day. 

It gets really bad when I look at my nephew. I just think about how he lost his dad, and... now he's stuck with me instead. It's hard to shake that.
Have you noticed that you feel down or lose interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with family?
I don't know. I guess I don't really have hobbies anymore. I just go to work and come home. It's... it's just what I do. I don't really feel much like doing anything else.
Do these flashbacks or moments where you feel like you’re reliving the accident happen frequently, and do they feel like they’re triggered by specific things you see, hear, or smell?

Yeah. I mean... like I said before, it happens a lot. And... yeah, the smoke, or the garage door. 

I don't... I don't really keep track of every little thing that sets it off. It just happens.
Have you been avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of what happened to your brother?

Yeah, I guess. I mean... I stay out of my own garage now. Unless I absolutely have to go in there for something. 

And... I stopped volunteering to do the electrical work at the church. Just didn't want to be around it. If people start talking about fixing up cars or... or the fire, I just change the subject or walk away. I just don't want to deal with it.
Do you find yourself feeling down or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with family?
Didn't you just ask me that? Like I said... I don't really have hobbies anymore. I just go to work and come home. That's about it.
Do you find yourself feeling emotionally numb or detached from people, even those you care about?
I don't know. I haven't really noticed anything like that. I just... keep to myself mostly.
Do you find yourself easily startled, on edge, or having trouble sleeping since the accident?

Sleep's... not great. Most nights I just lie there. Listening for... crackling sounds, I guess. Or a car door out in the driveway. 

And if I actually do fall asleep, I just jolt awake later. Completely soaked from... dreams. About the garage. Once that happens, I can't really get back down before I have to get up for work. So... yeah.
Do you find yourself having intrusive, distressing memories of the accident, or do you ever feel like you're reliving it as if it's happening all over again?

Yeah. Sometimes. I'll just be... I don't know, in the middle of wiring a panel at work. Or I'll be at my sister's and hear my nephew shut the garage door, and... it's like the job site or the house just drops out from under me. 

Suddenly I'm right back there. I can smell the smoke. I can see my brother. It just... happens.
Do you often feel afraid, guilty, or angry specifically about what happened to your brother, and does that feeling seem to never go away?

I mean... yeah. I guess. 

It's just this... heavy feeling. Like it just sits right in my chest, all day. A lot of... anger, I guess. And guilt. 

It's hard when I... when I have to look at my nephew. Just knowing he lost his dad, and... and he got stuck with me instead. So... yeah. It doesn't really go away.
Do you find that feelings of guilt or anger about what happened to your brother are always with you, even when you're not having flashbacks or remembering the accident?

Yeah. Like I said, it... it doesn't really go away. Doesn't matter if I'm having one of those memories or just... driving to work. It's just always there. 

I don't really know how else to explain it.
Do you find it hard to feel positive emotions like happiness or love, even when you're with family or doing something you used to enjoy?
I don't really know. I guess... I just feel kind of numb, mostly. It's hard to really feel much of anything lately.
Is there anything that used to bring you joy or happiness before this happened, that no longer seems to affect you now?

I don't know. I guess I used to like... fixing up old cars. Working on engines. 

But I haven't been out to the garage in a long time. Just... don't really care about it anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like eating much less or more than usual?
No, not really. I guess I eat about the same. Haven't really paid attention to my weight.
Do you find yourself thinking that you're a bad person, or that the world is unsafe, because of what happened to your brother?

I... I don't really know about the rest of the world. But... 

I just can't seem to shake this thought. I've been an electrician for years, you know? And... if all that experience couldn't even keep my own brother safe... 

I just figure I'm a danger. To anybody who works with me, or... or lives under my roof. I guess that's why I finally came in here.
